description: Iran severed relations with the US on 7 April 1980 after the revolution and the hostage crisis. Under the 1981 Algiers Accords each country named a third country as protecting power; Pakistan represents Iranian interests in the US.
source_name: Interests Section of Iran in the United States

aspect: It is a post box, not an authority
description: The Interests Section functions as a pass-through for most document requests, meaning it has limited ability to resolve anything locally. Applications are forwarded to Iran for the actual decision.
energy_note: Nobody you can reach has the power to help you.

description: Processing at the Interests Section alone takes 4-12 weeks, after which the file goes to Iran for final approval and printing. Total turnaround is typically 6-14 weeks.
time_note: Six to fourteen weeks, one document.

description: The Interests Section does not accept walk-in applicants for most services. Appointments, where offered at all, must be scheduled in advance - for a single office serving an entire country.
energy_note: One office. One country. No door.

aspect: EXAMPLE - address it to the right tenant
description: Guidance warns applicants to address materials to the 'Iranian Interests Section' and NOT to the Pakistani Embassy, despite it being the same building - and to use a trackable courier and keep copies of everything.
energy_note: Your life documents, in the post, to the correct sub-tenant.

aspect: EXAMPLE - even the address is contested
description: Published addresses conflict: older references give 2209 Wisconsin Ave NW, current ones 1250 23rd Street NW. The section operated on Wisconsin Avenue from 1981 to 2015 before moving into the Pakistani embassy building - so out-of-date guidance sends documents to a building that has not handled them for a decade.
energy_note: Posting your only passport to an address that may be wrong.
source_name: Interests Section of Iran in the United States

description: Renewal now begins with registration on Iran's Mikhak portal (mikhak.mfa.gov.ir) before any paper is sent - an Iranian government system that must be reached, and made to work, from abroad.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the scale of who depends on it
description: In 2003 the Interests Section reported holding passport records for roughly 900,000 Iranians resident in the United States, many of them US-born.
source_name: Interests Section of Iran in the United States
